title: Excessive Lifetime Contagion (Borrow Coupling)
pattern: Structs store short-lived borrow references (`&'a T`) instead of taking ownership, forcing every struct up the dependency chain to inherit and carry the lifetime parameter `'a`.
why_bad: It couples the lifetimes of all structs to the short-lived stack frame of the original source data. The structs can never be placed in background threads, event buses, or stored long-term.
detection: A struct hierarchy where multiple layers of structs all contain lifetime parameters matching the innermost primitive reference.
counterexample: Highly specialized local zero-copy parsers designed strictly for immediate, high-performance in-place parsing.
